posts.cooked:
Since Qualities and Powers are pretty broad reaching, I think the key to justifying the use of them is explaining how it works. 

"I imagine the shards of metal slamming into the spider-bot, and then 'woosh' they do." 

Against bots it'd be easier to justify "Metal + Technology" with "knowing what I know about robots, I have the shards of metal slam into a crucial actuator joint." 

Or if she's zapping people with electricity (like Brainstorm), I might say "I draw the power out of the city grid to zap the bad guy" (Tech+Electricity)  Or "I mentally generate a lightning bolt to zap the bad guy" (Creativity + Electricity). There's probably a good Science + Electricity explanation for zapping someone too,

posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked:
The OP mentioned using Metal and Creativity (rather than Metal and Technology), but the same issue applies.  Flinging a shard of metal at a target doesn't particularly represent a manifestation of either Creativity or Technology.

The word "creativity" implies using abilities in a novel or unorthodox manner, something new or beyond the norm.  Simply throwing metal shards at something-- even sharpened ones-- isn't either novel or unorthodox.  Nor does it represent any particular level of technology, beyond that of a sharpened shard.

A potential Creativity + Metal attack could easily exist, perhaps as something like,  "I'm going to take those two pieces of sheet metal and tekekinetically snap them shut around the creature like a bear trap" or "I'm going to swing that giant wrecking ball around like a flail and slam it into the creature."  But as it's described above, I'd probably rule the same as your GM: Metal + Ranged Combat (or Thrown Weapons, or Telekinesis, or some other attacking power/quality).

The case can surely be made for "Describe cool things, and then find dice for them," but what's being described in the original post seems more to be along the lines of "I want to use my best dice, regardless of whether they apply to what I want to do."  Not accusing or judging, here--there are surely ways to use the combo described above, but doing so seems like it should take more than "I throw metal at it. "

aramis:

Not everyone RPGing is there to tell a story. I know more than a few for whom RPGs are tatical sims. Even narrative-focused games. There are many different approaches to “roleplay” - and a surprisingly large number don’t involve being in Actor stance.

And that’s fine, provided that your group (including your GM) is on the same page.  There’s room enough for all types of rp out there.  I might question what kind of enjoyment a tactical, ‘crunch-focused’ gamer might get out of playing a game so heavily focused on narrative and story over mechanics, but there are a lot of types of enjoyment, so it may be something else entirely.

It definitely sounds like the GM in question wants a more finite justification in-game for the mechanical choices being made out-of-game, which seems to imply that they’re looking for a more narrativist approach–“Describe what you’re doing, and I’ll find a way to replicate that in dice.”  However, the disconnect seems to be difference in interpretation, stemming from the ultimate effect being produced.  The GM (and, frankly, myself) are probably looking at it like, “You’re controlling Metal, and using it as a projectile attack.  That’s Metal + Ranged Combat.”  I won’t speak further for that GM, but for myself, you’d probably have to come up with some more unorthodox or unexpected in order to use Creativity in place of Ranged Combat, such as the examples I provided above, if you were trying to convince me into using that dice pool.  It’s obviously possible to use that combo, just maybe not as a simple “shoot it with metal spikes” attack.

FTR, this is really only a problem when playing a pregen with a limited subset of the rules available. The full description of the standard Qualities (like Creativity) should explain just what Creativity covers. 

Qualities sort of seem like Aspects from Fate and require agreement as to when it applies. I might think that "Private Investigator" covers punching because PIs get in lots of fights. The GM might say "no, you need a separate skill for that" and we'd hash it out during character creation.

posts.name: JesterOC
posts.cooked:
As long as the narative fits the dice I'm fine with it. However if you have a quality or power that is a bit of a stretch, I think it is on the player to stretch it to fit.

Creativity + Metal had better involve creativity and metal. IMHO tossing shards at bots isn't really creative. Having the robots become hyper magnatized which makes them pull in metal from all around that will slam into them (including over nearby robots) does seem more creative.

I view the creative keyword is awesome because it is almost a catch all, but I feel that it must have a bad side or else you might as well not have any other quality. I figure that in game the player will be forced to think of new and creative ways to attack after a time. After a while an idea moves from creative to standard, how long does that take, I don't know, but I think the burden is on the player to keep chaning it up, so the GM doesn't have contemplate it.

If you don't want to be burdened with coming up with creative new ways to use your powers, swap it with ranged attack.

posts.name: jlabrecque42
posts.cooked:
I would say that yes, technically Unity is a technomancer, so she has the ability to telekinetically deconstruct metal and bend it to her will. However, as a GM, I would probably steer you away from launching metal shards at things because it doesn't fit her character.  Unity has honed her ability to have the precision to assemble highly functional robots that help her get things done.  While she may have the psychic ability to hurl metal at things, Unity as a character would look down on such a blunt solution. I think her affinity for her robots makes it more likely that she would construct a scorpion bot with a large stinger that could shoot it at her enemies.  Or even better, a porcupine!  Not nearly as efficient, but that is who she is. 

When I think metal + creativity, I think of constructing an earthworm bot that can fold itself into a key to unlock a door.  Again, not as efficient, but Unity will always make a bot to do a thing rather than do it herself.
